resources.string: Keeps the content filter switched on and stops it from being removed without the key.
read the chosen drawbridge policy and options
Let\'s draw the bridge on the toxic addictive internet and keep our peace of mind.
A raised drawbridge at sunset, between an autumn park where somebody is reading on a bench and a rocky shore where cartoon monsters are waiting.
This policy document offers nothing to choose from.
Apps this policy does not allow are removed straight away. Switching back later does not reinstall them.\n\nThe DNS resolver and the blocklists change with it.
Downloading blocklists and checking installed apps…

This policy is always active, also when drawbridge is unlocked. The options underneath are further restrictions and are active only when locked.
Every browser that works properly with the web filter. We recommend herald: it is minimalist, it shows a clear page when something is blocked, and it follows drawbridge\'s policy.
A minimalist browser for those who surf too much: it\'s by default monochrome, it scrolls and clicks more slowly, and has only one tab. Every other browser is removed.

Removes all browsers. Before locking this in, make sure all your apps are logged in, because some apps require a browser to sign in.\n\nAlso, know that some functionalities may break or not work, e.g. payments, QR codes, etc.
After the lock, no new app can be installed. The apps that are on the phone at that moment go on updating as normal.

Before locking, prune down your apps and keep only those you want to have on your phone. After locking, no new apps will be allowed. Updates of existing apps do come through, so keep the Play Store to update.

herald and anything else the policy requires are the exception. drawbridge installs those itself, from the signed policy you chose, and they arrive whether the phone is locked or not.

Leave this off if you are not sure. A blocked app can always be blocked later; an app nobody can install is a phone somebody has to come to you about.
drawbridge when unlocked allows all of the following. If you don\'t want some of these \u2018services\u2019, and rightfully so, disallow them and lock drawbridge.
This policy offers nothing to switch on.

The policy is inspired by best practices in digital minimalism and is a good choice for anyone, including adults. The ages are a recommendation by pediatricians and neurologists, and are only relevant for caretakers setting up a device for a teen.
That option is no longer in the policy.
Technical detail about this phone and how drawbridge was set up on it. Useful in a bug report — especially for a device or Android version nobody has tried before.
Could not reach the policy server

Locking will apply the restrictions other than the default, for both websites and apps.

You will be shown a random key, one which is difficult to remember and changes every time you lock. The key is needed to unlock drawbridge (outside of the timer). Write the key down and hide it carefully. Alternatively, you may ‘forget’ the key on purpose, e.g. when you set an unlock timer or if you want your device to have the restrictions indefinitely.

If Android asks you if drawbridge should run in the background, allow it. Drawbridge works either way, but allowing it allows timely updates.
The content filter has to be running before the phone can be locked.
We remind you the key is different every time.
A newer version of drawbridge is available.
This phone runs %1$s (build %2$d). Build %3$d is available.
This phone runs %1$s, which is the newest version the policy names.

Play Protect will block this update, and that is not a fault in either of them. drawbridge is allowed to install apps on this phone — it is how herald got here, and how blocked apps are removed. An app that can install other apps is exactly what Play Protect is built to be wary of, because on most phones nobody chose to give an app that power. On this one you did, when you set it up.\n\nPlay Protect cannot tell those two situations apart, so it stops the update. Pausing it for a minute is enough.
1. Open Play Protect and turn off scanning.\n2. Come back here and tap Install the update.\n3. Turn Play Protect back on.
Play Protect could not be opened from here. It is in the Play Store, under your profile picture.
Downloading and installing. This screen will say when it is done.
The phone refused the update, which is what Play Protect blocking it looks like. Pause Play Protect and try again.
Turn Play Protect back on afterwards. It is the only thing on this phone watching for genuinely harmful apps, and it does not interfere with anything else drawbridge does.
A key never contains the letters O, I or L. A round character is a zero. If you write one down ambiguously, typing O, I or l back still works.
I have written down or saved the key, or forgot it on purpose.
drawbridge key: %1$s\n\nKeep this somewhere safe and offline. It unlocks the drawbridge settings on the phone.
Type the key you were given when this phone was locked. Dashes and capitals do not matter.
If that does not match what you remember, this phone has been unlocked or reset since.
The lock ends on its own after the period you choose. You still get a key, and it still works.

When no timer is put, drawbridge will stay locked until you put the key. Optionally, you can put a timer for drawbridge to automatically unlock.

There will still be a key to unlock before timer runs out, but many people would rather ‘forget’ the key and just use the timer to get some time off, e.g. “4h of studying without internet”, “a weekend of camping offline”, “2 weeks without YouTube”, “3 weeks with a strict internet curfew”.

The period is fixed at the moment you lock. It cannot be shortened, extended or switched off from a locked phone, and the phone's clock is held to network time so the date cannot be moved either.
Locking will end by itself after %1$s.
Locking will last until you unlock it with the key.
This lock ends by itself after %1$s. You still get a key and it still works — the timer is only what happens if nobody uses it.
This phone unlocks itself %1$s after you tap Done, with or without this key. Until then the key is the only way in.
Somebody on this phone said the code was lost, so it unlocks by itself on %1$s. If you still have the code, unlock and lock again to stop that.

If you forgot the key but need drawbridge unlocked to change the restrictions or do a factory reset, you can start in the next screen a timer of %1$s. Drawbridge will then unlock.\n\nThe timer is shown on the lock screen, so it will be obvious.
drawbridge unlocks itself on %1$s. Until then nothing changes: the phone stays locked, and the code still opens it.
This phone already unlocks itself on %1$s, and that cannot be brought forward. Unlocking with the code before then ends it.

This lifts every restriction and stops the filter. Nothing is erased and no data is lost.\n\nThis is a one-way decision. If you want to reactivate the restrictions, this will require a fresh factory reset with a new drawbridge install!

The content filter, app blocking and all device restrictions will be switched off. Apps that were hidden become available again. No data is lost.

The record of how long this phone has been protected is cleared with it.

This cannot be undone from the phone. Switching the restrictions back on means setting the device up again from a factory reset.

After lock: No internet traffic possible. Only calls and SMS, as well as GPS reception and FM-radio when available.
Only allow internet between certain times. Recommended is at least a half hour per week to install updates.
The phone is offline between these hours.
